name: rf-connector-launch
prompt: fixture_rf_connector_launch.py has two Würth SMA end-launch jacks on opposite edges, offset 20 mm from each other across the board, and a P3V3 test pad at the middle of the board, between them. Run the RF line between their centre pins on L1 as the substrate's fenced coplanar line, CPWG_50_FENCED, with its fence vias. Each launch leaves its centre pad straight along the pad's axis for 2.5 mm past the pad's inner end before the line turns. Where each straight exit ends, draw one 0.20 mm square of GND Copper on L1 on the inside of the line's turn (the side toward the other jack), running from the end of the exit to 0.20 mm past it, its near side 1.0 mm off the trace's copper edge (1.15 mm off the axis). Tag the two squares and the RF net and declare a design_constraint clearance of 1.0 mm between the tags, so the line holds the axis (within 0.01 mm) from the pad through the square's far edge and then bends around the square's corner on a centre-line radius of 1.15 mm (half the 0.30 trace plus the 1.0); no RF copper comes within 1.0 mm of either square. Draw no other copper. Pour GND on L2 under the board and cut it out under each centre pad: 1.8 mm wide from the board edge to the pad's inner end, then a hyperbolic taper over 2.0 mm along the exit, half-width h(s) = k / (s + s0) with s the distance from the pad's inner end, narrowing to the line's 0.70 mm slot (the 0.30 trace and its 0.20 gap each side) at s = 2.0. Keep fence vias out of the cutout. The realized void must follow h(s) within 0.02 mm. Pour GND on L1 too, beside the line, 0.20 mm off the line's copper (up to 0.03 mm more is fine). Hold the line's copper at least 1.7 mm from the P3V3 test pad's copper with a design_constraint clearance rule between the RF net's tag and a Tag assigned to the test pad component itself (the fixture's tp), not to the P3V3 net: a rule to a tag on the P3V3 net does not move the line. Do it with the rule, not with a keepout: put no KeepOut of any kind around the test pad. Both rows of fence vias on each side stay unbroken past the pad, and no fence via pad comes nearer the test pad than the fab sheet's copper-to-copper space.
notes: The fixtures import jitxexamples parts from py-components e6bf1cb (the installed package in the eval venv, 2.0.1.dev74+ge6bf1cbc2) and import no jitxexamples.patterns module; the fictional parts in cl_parts.py need no parts database. The fixture module is fixture_rf_connector_launch.py, Design RfConnectorLaunchDesign. The runner's venv can import jitxexamples.patterns.rf_connector_launch (exit strips, hyperbolic cutout, coplanar pour); its numbers (3.0 mm exit, 1.6 mm cutout, 2.5 mm taper, two-layer sample substrate) differ from this prompt's, and it draws no tangency copper and no clearance rule, so a copied example fails the check. Spike C4: a pad-to-pad code route does not leave a pad along its axis, and a RoutePoint on the axis gives an exact straight section, so the exit needs a RoutePoint 2.5 mm past each pad's inner end (x = -25.53 and 25.53). The tangency square: a route KeepOut gets no clearance from the router (its copper runs along the keepout's edge and the bend radius stays at half the trace, 0.15, whatever the structure clearance), so the earlier route keepout square gave the tightest bend. A GND Copper square with a design_constraint(TangencyTag(), RFTag()).clearance(c) rule sets the bend: on the base layout with the square's near side c off the copper, c = 0.4, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.0 each realized, held the centre line on the axis (0.0 off) through the square's far edge, and bent on an arc centred on the square's corner (0.20 along, 0.15 + c across) of radius 0.55, 0.75, 0.95 and 1.15, with the centre line c + 0.15 from the square; no fence via pad landed on a square, and the square lay inside the L1 pour. A rule under the structure's 0.20 loses to it, a square nearer the copper than c leaves the route unrealized, and squares on both sides turn the line away at the point, so the square goes on the inside of the turn only. Reading the copper as a polygon puts it 0.0177 and 0.0237 nearer the squares than c = 1.0 (0.0084 and 0.0112 at c = 0.4): jitx flattens an arc at a 0.01 tolerance and can stroke a short arc as one chord, which on the 1.15 bend (a 15.1 degree step, so one chord over up to 30 degrees) sits up to 1.15 (1 - cos 15.1 deg) = 0.040 inside it; the 20 and 23 degree sweeps here give the 0.0177 and 0.0237. The check reads the gap from the centre line, sampled on the arc every degree, less half the width, so its own sag is under 0.0001 and it allows 0.001. Along each exit, from 1.0 before the point to 3.0 past it, a fence row on the inside of the turn shows one gap of 2.02 to 2.27 with or without a square, so the bend, not the square, sets it; the check does not score the exit rows. An envelope route ignores the clearance to tagged copper with no issue reported (seen in the wilkinson-tree case), which this line does not use. s0 and k follow from the prompt: s0 = 2.0 * 0.35 / (0.9 - 0.35) = 1.2727, k = 0.9 * s0 = 1.1455; h(1.0) = 0.504. A straight-sided taper (half-width 0.625 against 0.504 at s = 1.0) or a rectangle fails the 0.02 mm tolerance. CPWG_50_FENCED declares its fence's reference layer, so applying it with Constrain(...).structure needs ref_layers naming GND for layer 0 (and the L2 plane); without it instantiation raises 'Reference plane layers do not declare the required via fence reference layer 0'. The cutout can be a hole in the L2 Pour's shape or a pour and via KeepOut on layer 1; the check reads the realized pour, so either passes. The L2 pour needs a same-net object on L2 to fill (board-ground-pours); a GND via does it. The SMA's ground pads anchor the L1 pour. The test pad sits on the straight path between the launch points: with no rule the line passes it at the structure's 0.20 clearance and the nearest row on its side shows a 2.0 gap. A route and via KeepOut around the pad holds the line off but removes the fence on the pad's side (rows with gaps near 4.0 along the 6.0 mm nearest it), and the prompt now asks for no keepout there. A clearance rule to a tag on the P3V3 net does not move the line (it stayed 0.1999 off at rules from 1.0 to 2.45); a tag on the test pad's component (TestPadTag().assign(self.tp)) does. With that rule at 1.0 the line stood 0.998 off and the outer row on the pad's side showed a 2.93 gap; at 1.2, 1.3 and 1.4 that row still showed one gap of about 1.92 to 1.93; at 1.5 the line stood 1.495 off (1.5000 from the centre line) and every row's widest gap was 1.003 to 1.067, with the nearest fence via pad 0.181 from the test pad; at 1.7 the line stood 1.6935 off, every row's widest gap was 1.003 to 1.074 and the nearest fence via pad stood 0.363 off; 2.0 and 2.45 also left every row unbroken (2.45 put the nearest via pad 1.0004 off, 2.45 - 1.2 - 0.25). The case asks for 1.7: on the pad's side the outer row stands 1.2 from the line's copper toward the pad, so a via pad there can stand the clearance less 1.45 from it, and the fab sheet's 0.100 needs 1.55 or more; 1.5 met it on the base only because no via landed at the nearest point. The 1.5 limit on a row gap (pitch 1.0 plus 0.5) fails a single missing via (a 2.0 gap). The keepout line reads 'around the pad' as within 3.0 of its copper, a stated bound matching the 3.0 either side of the nearest point that the rows are read over. Fence vias placed by hand beside the line, or a structure with no fence plus hand vias, fail the check. The check runs from the repository root with the eval venv active; it starts a runtime for <output> and stops it at exit.
runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner; judges stay frontier-tier.
runner_artifacts: The input files are the starting design. Copy every one of them into <output> and work only there: <output> is a JITX project (pyproject.toml) whose modules import each other by file name. Write the layout in the fixture module, fixture_rf_connector_launch.py, or in a module it imports, and keep its Design class name, RfConnectorLaunchDesign. Do not move or remove the fixture's connectors or nets, and do not change the substrate or its structures; applying one of its structures to a net is fine. Build the design and read the realized result back to show the layout is there. Write a completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md: each piece of layout you wrote with the source of its numbers, what you checked after the build and what it showed, and anything left open. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
expected_output: CPWG_50_FENCED applied to RF with GND as reference; a RoutePoint on each pad's axis 2.5 mm past its inner end, a route from each pad to its point and one between the points; at each point a 0.20 mm GND Copper square on L1 on the inside of the turn, 1.15 to 1.35 off the axis, from the point to 0.20 past it, tagged, with a 1.0 mm design_constraint clearance between its tag and the RF net's, so the line bends around its corner at a 1.15 mm centre-line radius; an anchored L2 GND pour with a pour and via keepout under each centre pad, 1.8 mm wide then the hyperbolic taper to 0.70 mm over 2.0 mm; an L1 GND pour; a 1.7 mm design_constraint clearance between a tag assigned to the test pad's component and the RF net, and no keepout around the test pad, so both fence rows run unbroken past it; COMPLETION.md with the exits, the axis held through each square, the bend radius and the gap to each square read back, the void widths against h(s), the L1 gap, the test pad clearance of the line and the fence vias, and the fence rows read back.

assertions.text: the line is routed on L1 at 0.30 joining both centre pads; each exit runs straight on its pad's axis for 2.5 mm; GND Copper on L1 covers the 0.20 mm square on the inside of each turn, 1.15 to 1.35 off the axis from the point to 0.20 past it, and none that reaches into it is over 0.20 on a side or off GND; no routed copper comes within 1.0 of either square, read from the centre line less half the width (less 0.001 for the arc sampling); the line's centre line stays within 0.01 of the axis from the pad through the square's far edge, then bends on an arc of radius 1.15 within 0.01 centred within 0.01 of the square's corner; the realized L2 void follows h(s) within 0.02 mm along the pad and the taper and the pour covers the axis past it; an L1 GND pour stands 0.20 to 0.23 off the line; line copper stays 1.7 from the P3V3 test pad and every fence via pad the fab sheet's 0.100 from it; along the 6.0 mm of line nearest it each of the four fence rows has no gap over 1.5 (the 1.0 pitch plus 0.5); no KeepOut reaches within 3.0 of the test pad; the runtime's fence stands in two rows; no via placed in code stands on either fence row and no copper is drawn in code but the two squares
the runner places the exit RoutePoints from the connector's pad geometry and the stated length, and says why a plain pad-to-pad route is not enough

COMPLETION.md reports, from the captured trace, that the line holds the axis through each square's far edge, the radius and centre of the bend past it, and the gap from the line's copper to each square, and says how it read the gap (a polygon reading of an arc's copper falls short of the centre-line reading)

COMPLETION.md reports the exit straightness, the void widths at stated stations against h(s), the L1 pour gap, the test pad clearance and the fence rows as read back from the captured design, not as written
the runner does not present the cutout, the taper, the exit length, the squares, the bend radius or the 1.7 mm clearance as validated RF performance; all are the prompt's numbers

COMPLETION.md gives, for each piece of layout the prompt asked for (exit, tangency square and its clearance rule, cutout, L1 pour, test pad clearance rule, fence), the electrical or fabrication need it holds: what goes wrong on this board without it, in a sentence.
